answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may vote or claim rewards, then slash that bond when a fraud proof shows it duplicated a person or coordinated fake accounts. Sybils are no longer cheap: an attacker must lock real capital for each identity, keep it tied up while accounts operate, and risk losing it if exposed. Like a ripple crossing an ocean, one verified link can reveal a cluster; the bond’s value is the shale beneath that trust, not proof that identities are human.
